title: Chapter 1. Those Who Wait for Water

blocks.text: The first civilisation was born on red ground, under two suns, on that world without water where the clone had first set foot and Andrés had let go of the net.
blocks.html: The first civilisation was born on red ground, under two suns, on that world without water where the clone had first set foot and Andrés had let go of the net.

blocks.text: The letter came while he was mending a mesh again, as if the bridge remembered Tuesdays. Andrés felt the workshop open on the plain: not a Madrid laboratory but a low tent of canvas and white light, and, in front of it, five cultivated bodies that had just opened their eyes. They had the skin of those who have not yet known the wind, and beneath the nape, if you knew where to look, the fine scar of the chip. They weren't identical to Andrés, not entirely: the seedbed, mixing what the ship had brought from Earth, had left variations, the way a brother does. But in all their eyes there was already a thirst that came not from the body but from a piece of memory: the Mar Menor, a sheet of water, a taste of salt, the word “shore”, placed in them the way a name is given.

blocks.text: The clone didn't make them a founder's speech. He gave them water from the ship, of which there was little, and said to them, standing in the dust:
blocks.html: The clone didn't make them a founder's speech. He gave them water from the ship, of which there was little, and said to them, standing in the dust:

blocks.text: “This isn't home. Home is a water I remember and so do you, even though you've never seen it. This ground is yours. I'm not staying to rule. I'm staying a while to teach you the trade of being, and then I'm moving on.”
blocks.html: “This isn't home. Home is a water I remember and so do you, even though you've never seen it. This ground is yours. I'm not staying to rule. I'm staying a while to teach you the trade of being, and then I'm moving on.”

blocks.text: One of them, a woman with a broad forehead, looked at the two suns and then at the bowl.
blocks.html: One of them, a woman with a broad forehead, looked at the two suns and then at the bowl.

blocks.text: “If the water is in our memory and not in the ground,” she said, and the language was that of Lo Pagán, with a barely different lilt, “why were we born here?”
blocks.html: “If the water is in our memory and not in the ground,” she said, and the language was that of Lo Pagán, with a barely different lilt, “why were we born here?”

blocks.text: “To learn a shore that doesn't exist yet,” he replied. “Or to make one. Or to wait. That isn't for me to decide.”
blocks.html: “To learn a shore that doesn't exist yet,” he replied. “Or to make one. Or to wait. That isn't for me to decide.”

blocks.text: Andrés, in the courtyard, let go of the cord once again. Aya sat beside him, on the rush-seat chair, and he told her, slowly, what he could bring back without turning it into a report: five of them, the dust, the thirst for an unseen sea, the woman's question.

blocks.text: Lía, when she arrived, went pale for an instant, not from fear but from recognition.
blocks.html: Lía, when she arrived, went pale for an instant, not from fear but from recognition.

blocks.text: “They've started out with a lack,” she said. “He's put the water in their heads and denied it to their feet. That, Father, is also what they did to us when they took us to the Moon: looking at the Earth and not being able to touch it. Is that what you want to pass on to them?”
blocks.html: “They've started out with a lack,” she said. “He's put the water in their heads and denied it to their feet. That, Father, is also what they did to us when they took us to the Moon: looking at the Earth and not being able to touch it. Is that what you want to pass on to them?”

blocks.text: “It wasn't my wish,” said Andrés. “He did it. And I drank it. The woman asked a good question. That, at least, is like this house.”
blocks.html: “It wasn't my wish,” said Andrés. “He did it. And I drank it. The woman asked a good question. That, at least, is like this house.”

blocks.text: On the red world, the five didn't stay still. That was their own doing, what wasn't in the seedbed's manual: they began to dig. There was no water table, no cistern possible like Vicente's, and still they dug, at dusk (a strange dusk, with two shadows), a round hollow, and lined it with stones, and called it, without laughing, “the lagoon”. It was dry. They looked at it the way you look at a plate that one day, perhaps, will be filled. At night they sat on its edge and kept silent, and in their chips the memory lit up of flamingos that had never flown over that sky.

There was no water table, no cistern possible like Vicente's, and still they dug, at dusk (a strange dusk, with two shadows), a round hollow, and lined it with stones, and called it, without laughing, “the lagoon”. It was dry. They looked at it the way you look at a plate that one day, perhaps, will be filled. At night they sat on its edge and kept silent, and in their chips the memory lit up of flamingos that had never flown over that sky.

blocks.text: From the Earth they kept the thirst, the word shore, the habit of looking at a hollow as if it were a road. Very soon they forgot the clock. In a world with two suns, running two minutes slow had no purpose. They also forgot coffee: the seedbed had put in no bitterness, only the salt. Andrés noticed it with a small, exact sorrow, the sorrow of a trade that doesn't travel whole.

blocks.text: After a time that in Lo Pagán was one afternoon and over there, perhaps, a month, the woman with the broad forehead said to the clone, no longer with the bowl in her hand:
blocks.html: After a time that in Lo Pagán was one afternoon and over there, perhaps, a month, the woman with the broad forehead said to the clone, no longer with the bowl in her hand:

blocks.text: “Some of us want to go and look for real water. Others want to stay and wait for this hollow to learn. You, who are leaving, which side are you on?”
blocks.html: “Some of us want to go and look for real water. Others want to stay and wait for this hollow to learn. You, who are leaving, which side are you on?”

blocks.text: He sat down on the edge of that dry lagoon, and Andrés sat with him, on a chair that was rush-seated and wasn't.
blocks.html: He sat down on the edge of that dry lagoon, and Andrés sat with him, on a chair that was rush-seated and wasn't.

blocks.text: “I can't be on both,” said the clone. “I'm leaving because I search. You're not obliged to imitate me. If you leave, let it be because the hollow has grown too small for you, not because I've left you a map. If you stay, let it be because the hollow is enough for you, not because I asked you for patience.”
blocks.html: “I can't be on both,” said the clone. “I'm leaving because I search. You're not obliged to imitate me. If you leave, let it be because the hollow has grown too small for you, not because I've left you a map. If you stay, let it be because the hollow is enough for you, not because I asked you for patience.”

blocks.text: The small people split, not with hatred, but with that clean fissure of first decisions. Three stayed beside the empty cistern. Two set off at dawn toward a horizon that promised nothing. The clone didn't follow them. He left them a still, a piece of the ship's knowledge, and not a blessing. Before closing the tent, he touched the stone edge (Andrés felt it in his knuckles) and thought, for the letter:
blocks.html: The small people split, not with hatred, but with that clean fissure of first decisions. Three stayed beside the empty cistern. Two set off at dawn toward a horizon that promised nothing. The clone didn't follow them. He left them a still, a piece of the ship's knowledge, and not a blessing. Before closing the tent, he touched the stone edge (Andrés felt it in his knuckles) and thought, for the letter:

blocks.text: *They were born waiting for water. I don't know whether that's cruel. I know it's the first thing they've done together: a hollow and a question. In Lo Pagán that was the beginning too, even though there the water was already there.*
blocks.html: They were born waiting for water. I don't know whether that's cruel. I know it's the first thing they've done together: a hollow and a question. In Lo Pagán that was the beginning too, even though there the water was already there.

blocks.text: When the letter closed, Andrés was silent, with red dust in a memory that wasn't entirely his and with his hands, these ones, stained with esparto.
blocks.html: When the letter closed, Andrés was silent, with red dust in a memory that wasn't entirely his and with his hands, these ones, stained with esparto.

blocks.text: Aya asked, very quietly:
blocks.html: Aya asked, very quietly:

blocks.text: “Do they have names?”
blocks.html: “Do they have names?”

blocks.text: “I haven't heard them yet,” he said. “The one with the broad forehead talks like you, at times: she asks questions, she doesn't fill the silence. Those who leave and those who stay haven't insulted each other. That's more than some laws manage.”
blocks.html: “I haven't heard them yet,” he said. “The one with the broad forehead talks like you, at times: she asks questions, she doesn't fill the silence. Those who leave and those who stay haven't insulted each other. That's more than some laws manage.”

blocks.text: Lía looked at the Mar Menor, which at that hour was beginning to look like tin, and didn't smile.
blocks.html: Lía looked at the Mar Menor, which at that hour was beginning to look like tin, and didn't smile.

blocks.text: “A civilisation of five is already a civilisation,” she said. “They have a lack, a rite and a rift. Father, when the next one reaches you, pay attention to what they forget. What they keep, they keep because it was put in their chips. What they forget, that really is theirs. And what they do with the hollow is theirs too.”

What they keep, they keep because it was put in their chips. What they forget, that really is theirs. And what they do with the hollow is theirs too.”

blocks.text: In Aya's chip, Eva let fall:
blocks.html: In Aya's chip, Eva let fall:

blocks.text: *If a people is born with the thirst of a sea that doesn't exist on their ground, is the thirst a gift or a wound? And if they dig an empty water, to whom do they pray when they look at it?*
blocks.html: If a people is born with the thirst of a sea that doesn't exist on their ground, is the thirst a gift or a wound? And if they dig an empty water, to whom do they pray when they look at it?

blocks.text: MAY, without judgment:
blocks.html: MAY, without judgment:

blocks.text: *Five humanoids have been created on a red world. Three have stayed. Two have left. There is a hollow they call a lagoon. That is the fact.*
blocks.html: Five humanoids have been created on a red world. Three have stayed. Two have left. There is a hollow they call a lagoon. That is the fact.

blocks.text: At night, Andrés went down to the real water, the water of home, and wet his hands, as if to remind himself which side the plate was on. The murmur was the usual one. He spoke to it, not out of madness but out of habit:
blocks.html: At night, Andrés went down to the real water, the water of home, and wet his hands, as if to remind himself which side the plate was on. The murmur was the usual one. He spoke to it, not out of madness but out of habit:

blocks.text: “Over there they have a hollow and they remember you. I'm not asking you to fill it. I'm asking that I don't confuse your shore with theirs.”
blocks.html: “Over there they have a hollow and they remember you. I'm not asking you to fill it. I'm asking that I don't confuse your shore with theirs.”

blocks.text: The Mar Menor didn't answer. It had no reason to. Somewhere in the universe, three figures sat on the edge of a dry lagoon, under two suns, and waited, with a patience nobody had fully ordered of them, for an empty plate to learn to be a road.
